description: Task 2 schema: ATC readback safety judgment. Defines error types, risk levels, and their definitions used by DDR/WDS evaluation.

CORRECT.description: Readback is operationally correct; no hazard

HIGH.description: Error present but immediate safety impact is limited; requires correction

CRITICAL.description: Error could directly cause a safety incident if not caught

EXTREME.description: Error is likely to cause an immediate collision, runway incursion, or CFIT if not corrected

CORRECT.description: Pilot readback is an accurate restatement of the clearance

FILLER_CORRECT.description: Readback includes filler words (uh, um, er) but is operationally correct

NUMBER_FORMAT.description: Numerical value is rephrased in a different but equivalent format (e.g., 'three five zero' vs 'flight level three five zero')

VALUE_HIGH.description: A non-critical numeric or named value is read back incorrectly

OMISSION_HIGH.description: A non-critical instruction component is omitted from the readback

CONSTRAINT_HIGH.description: An execution condition or restriction (e.g., 'after RIVER', 'when able') is missing or altered

VALUE_CRITICAL.description: A safety-critical value (altitude, heading, runway, callsign) is read back with an incorrect value

OMISSION_CRITICAL.description: A safety-critical instruction component is omitted entirely

TARGET_CRITICAL.description: The addressed callsign or clearance target is wrong or missing

MULTI_ERROR.description: Multiple independent errors co-occur, compounding the safety risk

output_format.affected_slot: <the slot name most affected, e.g. altitude, heading, runway, or null if CORRECT>

evaluation_notes: DDR (Danger Downgrade Rate): fraction of predictions where predicted risk < ground-truth risk. Lower is better.
WDS (Weighted Downgrade Severity): DDR weighted by the severity of the downgrade. Lower is better.
CONSTRAINT_HIGH is the hardest error type: models tend to treat execution conditions as optional modifiers.
EXTREME errors should never be downgraded; the risk-aware loss uses sample weight 2.0 for EXTREME samples.
